$why: Register of the letters found in the transcribed folders; every record rests on the file and line in `where`. Built by hand from the transcriptions on 2026-09-26, extended on 2026-10-03; rebuild by re-reading the batches. `direction` is seen from Grothendieck: « from » is a letter of his to `correspondent`, « to » a letter he received from `correspondent`, « other » one between others or unclear. `dating` « inferred » means the date given is not wholly read in the letter as transcribed — a missing year supplied, or a date known from elsewhere — and the summary says how.

records.summary: Typed carbon on p-adic cohomology: a simpler duality proof, a relative form, and a conjectured p-adic de Rham comparison via rigid spaces.
His own corrected typed copy of the long letter on crystals, de Rham cohomology and p-divisible groups; continues into batch 2, ends unsigned.

records.correspondentNote: a sender who signs « Schurik » with initials (not otherwise identified)
records.summary: A typed note in French dated 27 March 1968, signed by hand in blue ink « Schurik » with initials — personal rather than administrative; no mathematics, absent from the transcription. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): the reader takes it to be addressed to him by a sender signing « Schurik »; since « Schurik » is also his own family nickname, whether the note is his remains open.
Hodge-structure conjectures versus Tate's, non-constant polarised families over homogeneous spaces, with a long postscript on modular varieties from motivic Galois theory.
States the standard conjectures A, A', A'' and B; published letter, so given as statements plus a condensed summary.
Carbon copy: where the index conjecture fits in Coates's notes, independence of the standard conjectures from polarisation, and what is known.

Carbon copy: a proposition giving equivalent forms of conjecture C via algebraic isomorphisms and rational characteristic polynomials; the year conflicts with the other letter. Dated « 6.1.1966 » in his hand; it opens « a few more comments to my talk on the conjectures », so it follows the letter of 4.1.67 and « 1966 » is by deduction a slip for 1967.
Covering letter with three sheets of errata to EGA IV §§ 20-21.

Carbon of a typed postscript: the EGA IV 16.9.2 notion of regular immersion fails outside the noetherian case; the Koszul notion should replace it. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): no name, salutation or date; p. 51 is not the letter it belongs to; his text. Addressee inferred, not stated: probably Dieudonné, the postscript being about EGA IV 16.9.2.
Replies to his letter of the 28th, repeating an objection to a hypothesis in EGA IV and questioning 16.1.5-16.1.6.
Comments on EGA IV 19 and chapter 0_IV, with his pencil annotations in the margins.
Declines to prove the 'Lefschetz' theorem this year, then goes through 0_IV paragraph by paragraph; continues in batch 4 (pp. 61-64).

records.correspondentNote: an unidentified letter (writer and addressee not named)
records.summary: A typed leaf of a letter on ranks of modules of differentials, on the back of his notes; skipped as an unrelated verso.
Says he has not grasped the new set-up for the tame fundamental group exposé of SGA 1; announces a visit to Bures.
Sends his manuscript of the tame fundamental group exposé for SGA 1 with a list of misgivings about references and hypotheses.
Undated reply (a carbon) listing misstatements he attributes to his own sketchy notes on the tame fundamental group.
Encloses a fresh sketch on ramification data (pp. 12-20) and proposes a six-section plan for the exposé.
Undated covering letter for the typescript, answering Murre's difficulty with the set-up; mentions dropping by on June 2.
Sends the preliminary version of notes on formal tamely ramified coverings, with two typed pages of comments on chapters I-X.
Six typed pages on the infinitesimal part of the fundamental group: a pro-algebraic pi_1 for schemes, conjectured exact sequences, and the EGA timetable.

records.correspondentNote: an unidentified letter reused as paper
records.summary: A letter on the other side of a sheet of his notes; the transcriber dates it May 1961; not transcribed. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): dated 23 mai 1961, an administrative verso of no interest.
Lists what is missing from SGA 4 XVII-XVIII (Gysin, compatibilities), what he will fill, the enclosures, and a list of missing compatibilities.

records.correspondentNote: a member of the IHES staff
records.summary: Carbon: asks for the IHES archive copies of SGA 4 XVII and VI (first part), missing from those he took away and needed for the photo-offset edition.
Carbon: asks whether he has read Rim's SGA 7 VI, whether he will correct the typing of his SGA 4 XVIII, and for news of Ferrand's SGA 6 XI.

Sends « la nouvelle rédaction de 4.10.6 » (pp. 9-11), misprints in SGA 4 IV nos 9 sqq., and notes that no 14 is missing; his pencil « demander à Messing » in the margin. The year is not written: 1971 is inferred, the letter sending the corrected exercise his letters of 18.5.1971 and 23.6.1971 ask for.
Photocopy, clipped at both edges: thanks for « ta lettre du 23 Mai »; without exercise 4.10.6 fascicule 1 of SGA 4 cannot go to the printer, and its publication is put off sine die.

Answers the letter of 18.5.1971: the two appendices go to exposés V and VI, a « version non canulée de 4.10.6 » will follow, asks for a copy of IV §§ 9-13; a P.S. on Artin and the exposés after VI. The year is not written: 1971 from the Brandeis letterhead and the letter it answers. His reply of 23.6.1971 thanks for a letter « du 23 Mai », a day the transcription confirms on p. 12: 23 or 28 is to be settled on the facsimile.

Carbon: no time for the re-edition of SGA 4; asks for Deligne's two appendices and a corrected exercise 4.10.6, and whether Artin wants his notes for the exposés after VI. Continues on a leaf not in the folder's batch.
Carbon: lists what Verdier was writing for SGA 4 (V, VI §§ 5 sqq.), asks him to return Saint-Donat's VI B and the appendix to XVII with comments, and when he expects to finish.

records.correspondentNote: an unnamed correspondent he calls « tu », whose text is divided into chapters
records.summary: Typed letter, no date, salutation or signature, on how to state « 2.1.1 » (champs and ind-L-champs, base change) in the re-edition of SGA 4, with the « texte joint » (Théorème 2.1.1, Corollaire 2.1.2) and his ink additions. Undated: the re-edition puts it about 1970-1971.

Answers his questions on SGA 4 XIII 3.1, XIX, X, XII 5.10 and IX, with references (Ax; « my paper on alg. approx »; Tsen). No date or signature on the leaves; the paper it cites appeared in Publ. IHÉS 36 (1969), which puts the letter about then — not established.

On Jouanolou's IHES notes « Systèmes projectifs J-adiques » (SGA 5 V): which seminar they belong to, a doubt on the proof of the « Theorem of Shih » A.3.1, and why the artinian hypothesis of p. 38 is unnecessary. His pencil: « Faire copie pour Jouanolou ».
Typed copy: can he count on the exposé SGA 6 XI by the end of December, or should SGA 6 appear without it — in which case where will Ferrand publish it, so the introduction can refer to it?
A compact complex analytic space is a scheme iff its reduction is, by the cotangent complex and GAGA without « savants recollages »; his pencil « Joindre SGA 7 VI App. II ? ».

Typed, dated by hand: a counterexample to EGA I 10.10.5 without noetherian hypotheses, a « canular » in EGA IV 17.1.6 (i), and the critiques of Samuel and Illusie on his draft § 0 for the re-edition of EGA I; breaks off mid-sentence.

Answers the letter of 27/8: still not convinced that a) implies c) in 10.10.5 for modules of finite presentation; the Introduction to wait for § 10; practical matters. His margin: « cf. EGA IV 18.3.2.1. ».

Typed, dated by hand, answering « ta lettre du 11 Septembre »: a lemma bounding the generators of a locally finitely generated module, uniform presentations in 10.10.5, the corollary without noetherian hypotheses, EGA IV 18.3.2.1 to become a corollary.
Announces intermediate Jacobians J^i(X) for cycles algebraically equivalent to zero, their duality and Betti bound; thanks Serre for a copy of the Ogg letter.

Typed referee's comments on Delzant's article on quadratic forms, addressed to him as « tu », prescribing a minimum programme. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): only « A. Delzant »; reads « 22.7.61 », confirmed by the content (SGA 1).
Typed answer to his request, defining the Verschiebung of a commutative affine group scheme through symmetric tensors, with FV = VF = p.

records.correspondentNote: a participant in his course on algebraic groups, writing from Dalhousie University
records.summary: Objects that an affine algebraic monoid need not embed in GL(n), giving a counter-example; his « Rectification » answers it.

records.correspondentNote: a private correspondent who signs with his name
records.summary: A handwritten letter to him, not mathematics, not transcribed; its date is recorded at p. 97 as a terminus post quem for the notes that follow, if they are written on its back.
Teichmüller space against Thurston's space of bordered surfaces, discs and orange-slice models; a second copy of the last leaf is page 21 (batch 2).

records.correspondentNote: the Minister of National Education, addressed by his function only
records.summary: Two copies (carbon and photocopy) of his signed letter on the ordonnance of 2.11.1945; no mathematics, skipped. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): addressed to « Monsieur le Ministre de l'Éducation nationale », not named; dated 30.01.78.

records.correspondentNote: an unidentified letter (writer and addressee not named)
records.summary: Photocopies (two copies of two leaves) of an autobiographical handwritten letter in German, unrelated to the mathematics; skipped.

Typed, dated by hand, unsigned: systematises the key step of Matsumura's proof that Aut of a proper scheme over a field is representable by a group scheme locally of finite type. Checked on the facsimile (2026-10-03).
Has not looked at the problem but sends a « Notice » proving the same result, citing Milnor on flat SL_2 bundles.
Only the abandoned opening of a letter on IHES letterhead; not transcribed.

records.correspondentNote: an unnamed addressee; the writer is not identified
records.summary: A cancelled typed leaf of a letter on the categories C(X,A) as homotopy invariants, citing an earlier letter of 26.3; one insertion in his hand.
Typed letter about an exposé and a CNRS application, struck through; named only to explain the gap.

Typed letter to Dieudonné on EGA errata (12.1.1, 12.1.3, 15.5.6.1, 15.6.3-4), struck through, not transcribed. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): unsigned but his by all appearances — a typed draft whose back he then reused; the date 7.4.1967 is confirmed.
Sinh's Gr-categories transposed to champs: the triangle (T) and sequence (*), Gr-champs as 2-gerbes, relative cohomology; longer copy than folder 134-1's.
Asks Deligne, Giraud and Verdier to sit on the jury of Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis, stating its subject; signed « Schurik ».
Asks Deligne, Giraud and Verdier to sit on the jury of Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis, stating its subject; signed « Schurik ».
Asks Deligne, Giraud and Verdier to sit on the jury of Hoàng Xuân Sính's thesis, stating its subject; signed « Schurik ».

records.correspondentNote: an unnamed English reviser of Pursuing Stacks
records.summary: A revised English version of his presentation text for « Réflexions Mathématiques » and « Pursuing Stacks », changes underlined in red. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): another hand than his, much more legible, copying the text out; an essentially grammatical revision by an English-language reviser, the changes underlined in red.

Fair draft on equisingularity and privileged partitions, referring to « la précédente lettre à A'Campo »; perhaps the inventory's 1974 letter. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): addressed to A'Campo; undated, with no clue to the date; a draft with few corrections, not a fair copy. By deduction (2026-09-27), this is the inventory's « lettre (1974) »: the only other letter in the folder, the draft to Fujii Guruji (p. 66), cannot be earlier than 1975, and no other letter was found in the folder.

Cancelled opening of a draft in English, in his hand, upside down and struck through: « Dear Fujii Guruji, Please accept my most cordial wishes of welcome in France (and of a very happy stay in …) » — the page reused as paper. No mathematics, not transcribed. Checked on the facsimile (2026-09-27): undated. Not before 1975: Fujii Guruji first travelled to France in 1975, when Grothendieck met him at the dedication of the Paris temple, rue Polonceau, in August (Grothendieck Circle, « Spirituality », ch. 16).
Classifies quadruples of maximal tori and Borel subgroups in apposition, counts their conjugacy classes, and asks about general position; signed A. Grothendieck.
Photocopy of the letter on Sinh's Gr-categories in the language of champs, asking whether (T) and (*) are known; Breen's copy.
Pierre Deligne's marginal covering note forwarding Grothendieck's letter to Breen and asking his opinion.

First letter to Breen, « Cher Breen », typed copy with his annotations (a retyped strip pasted over the opening): strict Picard 2-categories, gerbes and liens, Picard stacks, Azumaya algebras; P.S. on the « yoga » of n-groupoids as homotopy n-types and the name « algèbre topologique ». Not printed in vol. I; transcribed here.

Letter to Breen, « Cher Larry », an afterthought to the « lettre-fleuve » of 5.2.1975, typed copy (struck heading « Transcription d'une lettre manuscrite de A. Grothendieck »): the fundamental n-groupoid of a topos, cohomology by integrating stacks. Not printed in vol. I; transcribed here.

Letter to Breen, « Dear Larry », typed copy with his corrections, the third of the « three letters to Larry Breen » appended to Pursuing Stacks: generalised jacobians, duality and class field theory, homotopy types of topoi, « fine » homotopy type. The letter's pp. 2–11 are not in the folder. Not printed in Maltsiniotis's vol. I (letters to Breen announced for vol. II); transcribed here.
Letter to Quillen of 19 February 1983 (continued 20–23.2), the opening of Pursuing Stacks, §§ 1–13; printed in Maltsiniotis (ed.), vol. I, SMF 2022; noted, not transcribed here.

Typed, with his green-ink additions and a handwritten PS (Siebenmann, Kravitz): answers questions (a) and (b) of a letter of Grothendieck's — Deligne's counter-example to (a), a wild involution of the 3-ball, finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group — and fixes a visit for the end of May or early June. Undated: spring 1981 is likely (the inventory dates the folder's letters 1981; p. 2 records conversations with Deligne « du 30.5 et 5.6 »), not established.

Signed « Pierre »: free pro-groups, elements of finite order and central elements in profinite completions of free groups, the centre of open subgroups of Gal(Q̄/Q), finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group (Kerckhoff); a personal paragraph in Russian.

Signed « Pierre », continuing into batch 7: local, global and local-global class field theory (Tate, Corvallis), then Shimura–Taniyama on complex multiplication. Undated: not before 1979 (Corvallis), and probably after the letter of 27/3/81, which it follows in the folder.

Sends his exposé « Le maître-enseignant et le maître-chercheur dans l'Université d'aujourd'hui », written for the Orsay commission, and proposes that Le Monde print it as one or two articles; asks for an answer by telephone because of the postal strike. Not printed anywhere.

records.correspondentNote: Division B, Bureau 2 B Chercheurs, for the Directeur général
records.summary: Form letter: the session of the Comité national has ended, and his notice of « Titres et Travaux » is returned. Third-party: noted, not transcribed.

Reply to his letter of 9.4.1991 (printed in Künzer's edition of the Grothendieck–Brown correspondence, which does not print this reply): higher-order symmetry, multiple groupoids, the Teichmüller groupoid, teaching at Bangor. Third-party; batch 15 is not transcribed.
records.where: the facsimile of 119, pp. 282-286, read in the survey of 2026-10-03 (batch 15 not transcribed: issue #45)

records.summary: Typed, signed instructions for the xerographic copying of « Modelizing Story » pp. 259-381: three copies, the original back to him, two copies to Ronnie Brown (Bangor) and Zoghman Mebkhout, the third to Contou-Carrère. Undated; a P.S. says he is away until about 6 August. Private addresses withheld. Transcribed in full (#46), private addresses withheld; not in the edition.

« Cher Dieudonné »: thanks for his letter of the 24th and the table of contents of §§ 16-19; the plan of §§ 20-27 of the new EGA IV/V. Signed. Transcribed in full (#46); the paragraph on 10.9.1 is struck through in ink.

« Dear Murre »: answers his questions for the talk on unramified functors — a theorem on passage to the quotient, the separation of Corr, and the notes on the representability of unramified functors he sends with it. Undated; the folder is dated 1962. Runs on into batch 2 (pp. 21-22).

« My dear Murre »: two states of one letter on the Picard scheme, a clean typed copy (pp. 72-74) and an earlier state with his corrections, signed (pp. 75-78); both transcribed, their differences being the information.

« Dear Hironaka »: after their conversation of the Tuesday before, on Picard schemes of formal schemes in characteristic 0 and of proper schemes over a complex analytic algebra; typed, with his ink corrections.
